title: Apple Hacked Scam Support Calls
description: I have been receiving multiple calls from scammers and several today so I recorded a few in case you speak to someone so you know what they might tell you.  It looks like they are calling from an Apple Store, but they are not.  They will tell you people are logging into your account from other countries and and to go to: www.helpme.net.  If you get a call, just hang up.  Here are some tips from Apple to protect yourself. https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204759

textual.context: The source presents this as a recorded example of a call that the narrator describes as a scam; the caller's statements are not independently endorsed as true.
textual.potential_relevance: The claimed Apple support identity and account-compromise claim are linked to a request to visit an external destination, creating a concrete identity, action, and destination relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish who operated the call or website, whether the account was compromised, or whether any person accessed the site or experienced loss.

textual.observation: The caller asks the viewer to open a browser, enter a website address, and connect to an alleged Apple server so a technician can perform a security scan.

textual.limitations: No credentials, payment, software installation, permissions, or completed remote connection are shown in these records.
